title: System Drift
hook: You used to reply to every lead within an hour. Now it's whenever. Nobody decided that, it just slipped.
statement: Systems quietly degrade unless you maintain them.
explainer: Standards rarely collapse in one day. They slip a little each week until the slip is the new normal. Regular check-ins catch it while it's still easy to fix.
sop: Write down your original standard for one area, like response time.
Compare it to today and estimate the Loss of Structure as a %.
Count the months since you last audited it. That's your Time.
Reset to the original bar, or consciously choose a new one.
Put a recurring audit on the calendar.
equation_example: Loss of Structure is 20%, and Time is 4 months since you last checked. 20 ÷ 4 = 5% drift per month. Higher or rising means standards are slipping faster than you maintain them. Lower means things are holding steady.
question: Name one standard that's slipped lately and write down what the original bar was.
closing_statement: Standards you don't maintain quietly wear away.
caption:
Principle Nº 129: System Drift

You used to reply to every lead within an hour. Now it's whenever. Nobody decided that, it just slipped.

Systems quietly degrade unless you maintain them.
